earlier_scan.source_named: Namkung, Ju (ed.). 1996. Phonological Inventories of Tibeto-Burman Languages (STEDT Monograph 3, Berkeley) — includes Yimchungru phonology sketch; no online copy reachable. Also Kumar 1973 Hindi-Yimchungru-English dictionary

sources.citation: Gope, Amalesh. Faculty profile / CV, Tezpur University Dept. of Linguistics & Language Technology (c. 2021-2023).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: lists Gope & Raguibou (in press) 'An Acoustic Analysis of Tone in Yimchunger' in Patgiri, Gope & Sarangthem (eds.) [= the 2021 Tezpur volume, Glottolog title 'The Phoneme Inventory and Tonal Contrasts in Yimchunger', pp. 142-165] and an MA thesis: Ishita Goswami (2021) 'Interactions Between Tone and Phonation in Yimchunger - A Preliminary Study'.

sources.citation: Language in India (www.languageinindia.com), monthly issue indexes 2001-2026 (301 index pages crawled).
sources.note: No article on Yimchunger/Yimkhiung/Yachumi found in any issue index.

sources.citation: Shodhganga (INFLIBNET) thesis repository, queries Yimchunger / Yimkhiung / Yimchungru / Raguibou.
sources.note: No linguistics thesis on the language; hits are sociology (Arentula 2025, Nagaland Univ.), political science, education, folklore.

sources.citation: Centre for Endangered Languages, Tezpur University. Yimchunger documentation metadata (recording sessions 2018-2020, Kuthur and Shamator).
sources.note: Metadata only; several tracks labelled 'Tones' (phonology verification, recorded by Gope, Raguibou, Borah 2020). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Centre for Endangered Languages, Tezpur University. 2017. CFEL Annual Technical Report (March 2017). p. 14 'Yimchunger'.
sources.note: Nothing. Reports fieldwork at Kuthur (Tuensang), 1800 lexical items, and a consonant phoneme chart; tonal analysis not yet reported; no mention of stress.

sources.citation: Coupe, Alexander R. 2014. Strategies for analyzing tone languages. Language Documentation & Conservation 8: 462-489.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 471 fn. 12 lists Yimchungrü among eight Tibeto-Burman languages of Nagaland on which Coupe did fieldwork on lexical tone contrasts (only Khiamniungan has a rising contour tone) -- first-hand evidence the language has lexical tone, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Keoshu, H., M. B. Qngr & Y. Muremong Khiphuru. 1998. Yimchungru Azuru Khehum. (DLI scan, archive.org dli.language.0918).
sources.note: Reader in Yimchungru; nothing on tone or stress.

sources.citation: Namkung, Ju (ed.). 1996. Phonological Inventories of Tibeto-Burman Languages. STEDT Monograph 3. Berkeley: University of California. p. 444 'Yimchungrü' (compiled from Marrison 1967 p. 373).
sources.note: Nothing. Gives syllable canon (C)(r)V(V)(C), consonant and vowel inventories only; unlike most entries in the monograph there is no TONES field for Yimchungrü and no remark on stress.

sources.citation: Halemane, Lingadevaru & Y. Shahoto Kvz Yim. n.d. Adult Primer in Yimchungru. Mysuru: Central Institute of Indian Languages (DLI scan, archive.org dli.language.0082).
sources.note: Literacy primer in practical orthography; nothing on tone or stress.
